passages.passage_en2_reada_00: Researchers working with a city library examined whether it should extend weekend opening hours. They compared a pilot group with a similar group that continued using the existing arrangement. After 6 weeks, visitor numbers improved by 12 percent in the pilot group, compared with 3 percent in the comparison group. By contrast, book lending changed little in either group. The improvement was strongest among first-time visitors. The researchers warned that participation was voluntary and the observation period was short. They described the result as promising evidence for a wider trial, not as proof that the policy would work equally well everywhere.
